patch_description:
This implementation switches from a fixed many-vertex polygon hull to an affine-normalized reference triangle, which makes every determinant directly equal to triangle area divided by hull area. The search uses a deterministic active-constraint gradient ensemble: it identifies the lower-tail triangles, accumulates their signed determinant gradients at participating movable points, and proposes batched moves combining these directions with annealed noise. This is followed by strict minimum-area coordinate polishing using active triangle normals and stencil directions.

The approach retains the useful lower-tail idea from prior programs, but replaces random active-point perturbation as the primary engine with a constraint-driven subgradient method. The fixed triangular hull also eliminates hull-area bookkeeping and guarantees feasibility through simplex projection.
